description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of proactive preparation for expressive suppression and cognitive reappraisal, as well as neural activity during the subsequent regulation of negative emotions.

spans.text: Altogether, the primary goal of this study was to explore neural correlates of preparatory control associated with the purpose to suppress or reappraise upcoming negative emotions.

design.value: Event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging was recorded in 42 female participants during an emotion-regulation paradigm involving suppression, reappraisal and appraisal of negative high-arousing IAPS images, with separate cue and target phases.

spans.text: Using event-related fMRI, we investigated neural correlates while participants were anticipating reappraisal or suppression (proactive, cue phase), as well as while they were applying these ERS (reactive, target phase), all within the context of negative, high-arousing emotions.
A Likert scale allowed participants to rate how successful they were in regulating or appraising their negative emotions (1 = not at all to 4 = very good).
